correctness.rationale: The graph and burning quantifiers are explicit. Positive cases \(7\le n\le15\) are certified by concrete source sequences. Non-four-burnability at \(n=16,17,18\) is proved by exhaustive enumeration of all radius-\((3,2,1)\) ball centers, leaving at least \(2,4,5\) vertices respectively before the final singleton. The infinite tail \(n\ge19\) follows from the degree-three ball cap \(22+10+4+1=37<2n\). Three-round burning is excluded analytically for \(n\ge8\) and exhaustively for \(n=7\). The verifier reconstructs these checks from the graph definition.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 work treats generalized-Heawood burning but announces exact girth-six values only on \(H(2k,k)\). The fixed-diagonal \(H(n,5)\) family is a natural entire girth-six subfamily, and the exact four-round cutoff isolates the transition between explicit four-source schedules and a provable obstruction. The result is not a routine single-instance computation: it combines an infinite degree-growth argument with the only three finite boundary cases and a complete positive interval.
